DeLorean Goes Flying for Real, Enters Airspeeder International Series as a Constructor
8 photos
Photo: DeLorean
When it comes to carmakers, they don’t get a lot more iconic than DeLorean, even though the brand was never commercially successful. Still, to have them enter a sky-bound racing series as a constructor is a pretty big deal. Meet the DeLorean Airspeeder Team that will take to the skies this November!
DeLorean joins a motorsport built on electric propulsion, advanced flight controls and AI-enabled safety systems. I think Doc Brown would be proud.
Speaking of being proud, DeLorean Motor Company is officially the first-ever American constructor in flying car racing, which is worth certain considerations. It’s not Ford or GM, but a brand that’s been associated with flying since the 80s – albeit only in pop culture.
Meanwhile, the final aircraft design, pilot line-up and full schedule will be revealed soon, ahead of the season opener. And yes, where they're going, they won't need roads. Just had to say it.
“DeLorean has always stood for the courage to imagine transportation differently,” stated company exec, Cameron Wynne. “People have pictured a DeLorean in the sky for forty years. We decided it was time to stop picturing it.”
Meanwhile, Airspeeder founder and CEO, Matt Pearson, had this to say: “DeLorean is the original flying car brand. Long before anyone had built one, the whole world already knew what a flying DeLorean looked like.”
"Every great racing series is defined by the constructors who choose to compete in it. To have an American icon line up on our grid in our first international season tells you where this sport is going. America has repeatedly changed how the world moves, on the road, in the air and beyond, and the DeLorean Airspeeder Team carries that ambition into a new arena.”
How does this work? In the Airspeeder International Series, constructors get to race electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft in three dimensions through electronically defined courses, as opposed to a conventional circuit.
Photo: DeLorean For its debut season, DeLorean will race the Airspeeder Mk3C, but for the 2027-28 season, the company will design a new aircraft in collaboration with student engineering teams at universities across the United States – including the University of California, collaborators at UC Berkeley and Georgia Tech.
As far as I’m concerned, this is way more than just a PR stunt. This is a genuine racing program with actual pilots. However, it remains to be seen how far air mobility can progress in the coming decades outside of special racing events such as this one. I still don’t think we’ll be seeing anything resembling Doc Brown’s flying DeLorean any time soon, if ever.
Is it impossible? No. Just highly improbable. At least for this century. In order to get "there", you'd need a completely revamped infrastructure, fully autonomous eVTOLs , and a complete shift in public perception about cars in general.
